---
title: "Optimal reports along the withholding-cost path"
subtitle: "2.5 · after the postrank theory book, ch. 10 and 22"
description: "The lower envelope of affine report-risk functions and its change points."
---

Each fixed report's posterior risk is a straight line in $\tau$ whose slope is the share of withheld pairs. The lower envelope traces the minimum-risk report across $\tau$, bending wherever the optimal report changes.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Overview.** The unrestricted optimum states 14 pairs (risk .0372), compared with .0417 under the three-grade cap. Open **Complete path** for exact intervals.
- **Before the first bend.** The report states 0 of 15 pairs, with withholding cost .0005.
- **Small cost, coherent report.** The optimum states 12 of 15 pairs, including 2 directions whose error exceeds $\tau$ because grades are chosen jointly.
- **Exactly at a bend.** At $\tau \approx .144$, 2 reports share the smallest risk where neighboring segments meet.
- **Three-grade cap.** At $\tau = .40$, the capped report states 12 of 15 pairs (risk .0817) while the unrestricted optimum reaches .0480.

<details>
<summary>Model assumptions and endpoint notes</summary>

The six fictional site posteriors are normal and specified for teaching. An independent three-unit equal-mean example illustrates reports that minimize risk only at a single endpoint $\tau = .50$ without occupying an interval of positive length.

</details>

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="In postrank"}
```r
library(postrank)
g <- c(A=1L,B=2L,C=3L,D=3L,E=4L,F=5L)
postrank_evaluate(g, pr_tutorial$one, weights=c(score_A=1), tau=.2)$weighted_risk # .03717176
```
The call evaluates the displayed report at a fixed cost.
:::

Standalone: [the τ path](../../embed/tau-path.html), for example `?tau=.005&zoom=low`.
